metric.why: Transformer and switchgear lead times stretched from months to years and now gate construction schedules as hard as permits do. Lead-time surveys are published by industry groups and research firms; watch the directory sources.
metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Critical equipment lead times now gate data center construction schedules as hard as permits do.

The metric tracks order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators. These are the physical inputs a data center cannot open without. When their lead times stretch from months to years, the constraint on new AI compute shifts from capital and land to the industrial supply chain that produces the equipment.

For AI specifically, this matters because compute capacity is downstream of buildings and power, and buildings are downstream of equipment that must be ordered years ahead. A hyperscaler can fund a campus quickly, but it cannot compress the queue for a transformer. Capital expenditure figures and colocation rental rates, the two sibling metrics, describe money and price. This metric describes time, which money cannot always buy.

The data does not give the lead times themselves, only the definition of what is measured and the claim that they stretched from months to years. It names no manufacturers, no current wait figures, and no dates for the shift. It also does not establish how much of total construction delay is attributable to equipment versus permitting, power interconnection, or labor.
